title: Define the source-clause semantic IR and completeness contracts
description:
Define the intermediate representation and the required completeness contracts
that every mechanics-bearing clause must satisfy.

Root cause: no semantic unit smaller than the record exists, so partial
projection is indistinguishable from complete projection.

Every clause must carry: stable clause identity; exact source span or spans;
semantic owner and record owner; clause kind; trigger and eligibility predicates;
activation / action-economy cost; targets and geometry; checks, attacks, saves,
and mutually exclusive alternatives; success, failure, and partial-success
branches; damage, healing, grants, ledger changes, and state transitions;
duration, recurrence, repeat checks, immunity windows, and termination; execution
owner and required engine capabilities; readiness disposition; regression
evidence.

Completeness contracts are required for: attacks, saves, checks, branches,
action economy, resources, durations, state transitions, geometry, choices,
variants, entity lifecycles, ledgers, and model adjudication.

Closes findings: SOL-001 (partial), F-06 (phantom resources — contract for
resource existence), F-27 (alternatives are first-class), CAP-001 (partial),
Opus residual "unverified effects semantics".

## REVIEW CONTRACT

Protocol: eshyra-clause-review-v1

Current normative obligation set for `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.1` / PR #475. Rewritten
2026-07-27 for the REDUCED scope. Supersedes every earlier revision on this bead
in full; superseded text and round-by-round history live in this bead's notes.
Requirements belonging to obligation authority or aggregate closure are NOT in
this contract — they moved with the code.

### Scope of this PR
This PR delivers the per-clause completeness contract ONLY.

Removed 2026-07-27 under the second churn stop, user-approved:
- obligation AUTHORITY — registry construction and validation, immutable facet
  and record authority, the evidence taxonomy including
  known-missing-source-clause, multi-part evidence capture, identity uniqueness
  across synthetic scalar and projected atom IDs — owned by
  `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.12`, blocked on a real source census (`eshyra-s38f`);
- SCOPE and AGGREGATE CLOSURE — branded scopes proving authoritative membership
  and record ownership, closure evaluating the same contract as per-clause
  evaluation — owned by `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.13`.

Rationale: the registry was asked to be authoritative while nothing underwrote
its authority, because the source census is deferred. `obligations.ts` is now a
13-line non-authoritative `ObligationSource` lookup interface; no validating
stub remains that could read as authoritative while proving nothing.

### Source obligation
- The clause references an obligation by `obl:::<sourceRef>:::<locator>:::<facet>`.
- ONE OBLIGATION PER CLAUSE is the load-bearing invariant. A clause discharges
  exactly one source obligation; that obligation may carry many facets. Source
  material with separable mechanics decomposes into multiple clauses.
- An obligation reference that does not RESOLVE must fail closed on every
  dimension it feeds. A missing or unknown obligation ID may never yield a
  satisfied dimension.

### Per-clause representation
- Composable facets, never universal clause-kind assumptions. A specialized
  facet transitively implies its base mechanic, so `save-with-damage` cannot
  certify `saves: []`.
- `duration`, `recurrence`, `repeatChecks`, `immunityWindows` and `termination`
  are canonical facets, required exactly when an obligation declares them.
- Canonical base requirements — `identity`, `sourceSpans`, `provenance`,
  `semanticOwner`, `recordOwner` — apply to every obligation, cannot be removed
  or overridden, and extensions are additive only. No caller-supplied contract
  can weaken them.
- ALTERNATIVES MUST FORM A COMPLETE PARTITION. For `choice` and `variant`, at
  least one alternative is insufficient: the exclusion graph must be symmetric
  and fully connected across the alternative set. A disconnected graph is not a
  set of mutually exclusive alternatives.
- EVIDENCE EQUALITY MUST BE ORDER-INDEPENDENT. Structural comparison, not
  serialized-string comparison; two evidence values differing only by property
  insertion order are the same evidence.

### Readiness dimensions
- CAPTURED, PROJECTED, SUPPORTED and DISCOVERABLE report INDEPENDENTLY. A clause
  may be semantically complete and unsupported; that distinction is the point.
- CAPTURED is satisfiable only by `source-span` or `authoritative-input`
  evidence tied to the obligation. `audit-finding` and
  `known-missing-source-clause` evidence identify a gap and can never close one.
- Capability resolution failures report against SUPPORTED, never PROJECTED.
- `EngineCapability` is the closed union `engine:F1`..`engine:F10`. Owning beads
  are the family epics under `eshyra-olc5`, which retain historical
  `eshyra-o9bd.19.5.*` IDs, so ownership is judged by actual bead identity and
  never by ID prefix.
- Resolvers (`CapabilityResolver`, `SourceEvidenceResolver`, `DiscoveryResolver`)
  are injected interfaces with test doubles, so the evaluator consumes evidence
  it cannot forge. Real implementations are out of scope.

### FAIL-CLOSED IS THE DEFAULT
Five fail-open defects have been found in this program: two registry closure
predicates, a ledger closure predicate, a prose guard, and CAPTURED satisfying
on an unresolvable obligation. The recurring idiom is returning an empty failure
list when a lookup does not resolve, so "no failures" reads as "satisfied".
Any evaluation path that cannot resolve its input must FAIL, never return empty.

### Approved residuals — owned elsewhere, not defects here
- exact source VALUES and relationships — `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.10`
- obligation authority — `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.12`
- scope and aggregate closure — `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.13`
- producer and readiness-gate integration — `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.1.2.1`
- production census and real resolvers — `eshyra-s38f`
- cross-PR identity adapters or parity tests — `eshyra-gvzx`
- source ambiguities — `eshyra-jhpt.6` / `.7`
- the `model-adjudication` facet
- importer migration, corpus recompilation, engine registry implementation

### Closure evidence
- Permanent regression evidence: `packages/core/test/clauseIrContracts.test.ts`
  and `packages/core/test/clauseIrObligations.test.ts`, including an
  unremovable base-requirement removal matrix and generated removal tests for
  every specialized facet.
- Finding-registry aliases: `indep:001`, `opus:F-06`, `opus:F-27`, `sol:CAP-001`.

### Cross-PR integration boundary — actual state
`obligationId` is `obl:::<sourceRef>:::<locator>:::<facet>`. PR #477 emits and
validates the same shape for genuine source obligations and keeps evidence items
in a separate `ev:::` namespace, so #475 and #477 are mechanically joinable.
PR #476 does not participate: it uses
`MembershipIdentity{recordKey, clauseId?, path?, sourceSpan?}` with no
`obligationId`. Bridging it is `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7`.

### Material contract changes 2026-07-27
1. Scope reduced to the per-clause contract; authority and closure requirements
   REMOVED rather than annotated, since the code moved to `.12` and `.13`.
2. Unresolvable obligation references must fail closed on every dimension.
3. `choice` and `variant` alternatives must form a complete partition.
4. Evidence equality must be structural and order-independent.

Prior review approval does NOT survive these changes. A fresh full review is
required.
design:
*** SCOPE GUARD — DO NOT BUILD A UNIVERSAL RULES DSL ***
The universal layer is ONLY: source-clause identity; semantic ownership;
completeness requirements; alternatives and branching; provenance; capability
requirements; readiness state. It does NOT require every D&D mechanic to compile
into one fully generic runtime language.

A1 must explicitly PERMIT all of:
  * shared normalized primitives (19.1.2);
  * kind-specific composition on top of them;
  * curated, source-backed specifications;
  * explicit unsupported or adjudicated clauses;
  * and forbid exactly one thing — SILENT PARTIAL PROJECTION.

THE DECISIVE RULE: when a projector recognizes that a deterministic clause exists
but cannot completely represent it, it MUST emit an explicit incomplete clause and
fail the appropriate gate. It must never produce a superficially valid partial
record. Family-specific projectors and curated specs remain appropriate; the
reviews support shared primitives for repeated structures (saves, attacks, damage
branches, geometry, duration, resources), not universal genericity.

TYPE GUARD: this bead may remain a TASK only while it is strictly an ADR /
schema-contract deliverable. If it also implements schemas, migrations,
validators and fixtures, convert it to an epic with separate design and
implementation children before starting.
acceptance_criteria:
- A clause cannot be classified complete from atom presence; completeness is evaluated against its kind's contract.
- Each clause has stable identity, exact semantic ownership, source spans, required fields, and execution disposition.
- The contract distinguishes captured, projected, engine-supported, and discoverable as four independent dimensions.
- Every mechanics-bearing record family (rule, feature, spell, creature, hazard, equipment, magic-item, ancestry, background, condition, action, feat, class, subclass, table) has a documented clause-completeness schema.
- Records are expressible as materialized views that group clauses, with no loss of the current consumer surface.

*** CORRECTION 2026-07-25 — DO NOT COLLAPSE THE FOUR DIMENSIONS ***
The first dispatch spec for this bead told the implementer that "a clause that is
CAPTURED + PROJECTED but not SUPPORTED does not evaluate complete". That
instruction was WRONG and PR #475 review caught it.

It conflates two different questions:
  * SEMANTIC COMPLETENESS — is the projection of this source clause complete?
    Answered by CAPTURED and PROJECTED.
  * READINESS / GREEN — can the clause execute end to end? Answered by the
    nine-point green definition, which additionally needs SUPPORTED and
    DISCOVERABLE plus an engine implementation and conformance tests.

ADR 0020 requires the four dimensions to fail INDEPENDENTLY and forbids any gate
collapsing them. A fully captured and projected clause awaiting an engine or
lookup path is not "incomplete" — it is complete-but-unsupported, which is
precisely the distinction the audit needed and the pack lacked. The nine-point
green bar still governs the FREEZE gate; it must not be smuggled into the clause
completeness evaluator.

## REVIEW CONTRACT

Protocol: eshyra-clause-review-v1

Migration baseline recorded 2026-07-26 during the final pre-protocol review
cycle. Derived from the corrected design at commit 1b33b18, not from future
infrastructure. Supersedes earlier prose in this bead where they conflict.

### Source obligation
- Source membership: the records in ObligationRegistry for the scope under
  evaluation. NEVER the set a projector happened to emit.
- Membership derivation: ObligationOrigin is a closed union of
  'source-extraction' | 'curated-specification' | 'audit-finding'. It cannot be
  'projector' by construction, so the producer of an artifact can never be the
  authority for which obligations existed.
- Source spans or authoritative inputs: ObligationEvidence, kinds 'source-span'
  and 'authoritative-input'. Origin-specific evidence is validated at registry
  construction; obligationId is obl:<sourceRef>:<locator>:<facet>.
- Complete obligations covered: this PR defines the obligation BOUNDARY, the
  facet vocabulary, and closure evaluation. Enumerating the SRD corpus's
  obligations is eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1 and is deliberately out of scope.

### Pack or artifact representation
- Required semantic distinctions: composable semantic facets, never universal
  clause-kind assumptions. save-with-damage and save-without-damage are both
  representable; the obligation states which facets the source demands.
- Branches and alternatives: branch predicates plus field-group predicates with
  minCount/maxCount for genuinely mutually exclusive alternatives.
- Timing, lifecycle, and termination: duration, recurrence, repeatChecks,
  immunityWindows and termination are required exactly when the obligation
  declares those facets, and never by blanket kind assumption.
- Provenance and ownership requirements: identity, sourceSpans, provenance,
  semanticOwner and recordOwner are canonical base requirements that no caller
  can remove; extensions are additive only.

### Cross-kind and cross-surface checks
- Related kinds or subsystems: all fifteen mechanics-bearing record families
  carry applicability contracts; facets are shared across kinds so a mechanic
  cannot be modelled twice with divergent semantics.
- Corpus-wide predicates or reconciliation:
  evaluateObligationClosure(registry, clauses, scope) reports satisfied /
  claimed-incomplete / UNCLAIMED. Family applicability, obligation membership,
  per-obligation completeness and aggregate family closure are four distinct
  concepts and are kept distinct in types.

### Engine capability
- Required capabilities: requiredEngineCapabilities, qualified engine:F1..F10.
- Existing owner beads: the ten family epics under eshyra-olc5.
- Known missing capability handling: readiness 'supported' binds to a capability
  identity and its owning bead through an injected CapabilityResolver, and FAILS
  when the reference is unresolved, unowned or stale. Self-attestation is not
  representable.

### Reference execution or executable proof
- Real artifact or pack-driven scenarios: deliberately out of scope. This PR is
  design/type-contract only; resolvers are injected interfaces with test doubles
  so the evaluator consumes evidence it cannot forge.
- Negative and fail-closed scenarios: adversarial tests T1-T8 in
  clauseIrObligations.test.ts, each named for the threat it defeats — undeclared
  obligation, narrowed kind, weakened requirements, permissive contract,
  readiness self-attestation, contradictory facet contract, family-array
  substitution, unknown contract selection.
- Replay, rollback, or determinism requirements: none in this PR; they belong to
  engine certification under eshyra-olc5.2.

### Approved residuals
- Source ambiguities: the three deliberate ambiguities remain under
  eshyra-jhpt.6 / .7 and are not engine defects.
- Deliberately model-adjudicated boundaries: the 'model-adjudication' facet.
- Explicitly unsupported scope: importer migration, corpus recompilation, and
  implementation of the engine capability registry.

### Closure evidence
- Generated membership query: evaluateObligationClosure over a registry scope.
- Permanent regression evidence: packages/core/test/clauseIrObligations.test.ts
  (T1-T8) and packages/core/test/clauseIrContracts.test.ts, which also preserves
  the three earlier fixed classes — requirement cardinality, independent
  readiness dimensions, non-mutable disposition.
- Finding-registry aliases: indep:001, opus:F-06, opus:F-27, sol:CAP-001.

### Material contract changes in this cycle
1. Obligation authority moved OUT of the clause into a registry with a
   non-projector origin. Reason: the producer defined the standard its own
   output was judged by, so an omitted or misclassified source clause vanished
   before evaluation.
2. evaluateClauseCompleteness no longer accepts a caller-supplied contract.
   Reason: an empty custom contract certified anything.
3. Universal clause-kind requirements replaced by composable facets. Reason: the
   save contract required damage, making a damage-less save unrepresentable and
   pressuring projectors to misclassify.
4. Readiness booleans replaced by inspectable evidence with injected resolvers.
   Reason: self-asserted SUPPORTED/DISCOVERABLE is not proof.
5. Family closure separated from family applicability. Reason: an array of
   supported families never established that their obligations were enumerated.

Prior review approval does NOT survive these changes. A fresh full review is
required.
*** CHURN STOP RULE TRIGGERED 2026-07-26 — PR #475 DECOMPOSED, NOT PATCHED ***
Fresh full review at 8c027f1 found further defect classes after the previous
round had already produced new invariant classes. Per the rule, no further local
review-patch cycle. Decomposition applied instead:

  eshyra-o9bd.19.1.10  Model exact source values and relationships in the
                       obligation authority. THE ROOT ISSUE: the authority
                       describes semantic SHAPES, not exact source VALUES and
                       relationships. Wrong ability/DC/damage/target-count/
                       duration-unit/reset-timing all pass a shape-only contract.
                       Encoding them needs a source-value model (typed scalars,
                       units, dice expressions, ability refs, inter-atom
                       relations) plus its extraction — a different problem from
                       the clause/obligation BOUNDARY, which this bead has now
                       largely got right. This is what kept dragging #475 back.
  eshyra-o9bd.19.1.11  Bounded mechanical defects: capability failures reported
                       against PROJECTED instead of SUPPORTED (the exact
                       dimension conflation ADR 0020 exists to prevent); wrong
                       bead-ID prefix in ownership checks; under-validated
                       evidence/provenance; branch and alternative bindings that
                       cannot target scalar mechanics; and ADR 0020 contradicting
                       this bead's contract about the #475/#477 boundary.

RETAINED HERE: the clause/obligation boundary — one obligation per clause,
canonical base requirements, facet implication closure, identity bound to
evidence, opaque validated scopes, CAPTURED restricted to source evidence,
closed engine capability identity, deep-frozen artifacts. That core survived
review and is what this PR should be judged on after rescoping.

A NEW CONTRACT and a fresh full review are required before this PR advances.

was replaced by a single current statement of the rescoped obligation set. The
superseded text is preserved verbatim below so the round-by-round history is not
lost.

### Invariant classes added 2026-07-26 (contract-grounded review at 1b33b18)

These are now normative and are what the next fresh full review must test.

- **ONE OBLIGATION PER CLAUSE.** The load-bearing invariant. A clause discharges
  exactly one source obligation; an obligation may carry many facets. Where a
  source sentence holds separable mechanics it decomposes into multiple CLAUSES.
  Enforced in the evaluator (`missing-obligation-reference`,
  `multiple-obligation-references`). This is what makes per-obligation
  evaluation sound: obligations can no longer share a clause-global atom, and
  hoisting option-local mechanics now fails validation.
- **CANONICAL BASE REQUIREMENTS ARE EXECUTABLE.** identity, sourceSpans,
  provenance, semanticOwner and recordOwner are validated for every obligation
  and cannot be removed or overridden, with an adversarial matrix that corrupts
  each in turn. They had been lost when facets replaced kind contracts.
- **FACET IMPLICATION CLOSURE.** A specialized facet implies its base mechanic
  transitively (`FACET_IMPLICATIONS`), so save-with-damage cannot certify
  `saves: []`. Generated removal tests cover every specialized facet.
- **TIMING VOCABULARY IS COMPLETE.** `recurrence` and `immunity-window` are
  canonical facets, not caller-side extensions.
- **ALTERNATIVES PROVE EXCLUSION.** The exclusion graph is validated for symmetry
  and partition; branches and alternatives bind to projected atom identities.
- **IDENTITY IS BOUND TO EVIDENCE.** Every component of an obligationId is
  validated against origin-appropriate evidence; synthetic locator divergence is
  rejected; repeated clauses at one anchor carry a stable occurrence locator.
- **CLOSURE CONSUMES AN OPAQUE VALIDATED SCOPE** and enforces exact
  family + record ownership; a raw scope literal cannot be passed, and a clause
  from another record cannot satisfy this scope.
- **CAPTURED REQUIRES SOURCE EVIDENCE.** Only source-span or authoritative-input
  evidence satisfies CAPTURED. audit-finding and known-missing-source-clause
  evidence identify a gap and can never close one.
- **ENGINE CAPABILITY IS A CLOSED IDENTITY.** `EngineCapability` is the union
  engine:F1..engine:F10, validated, with the two capability-evidence surfaces
  reconciled so stored evidence cannot drift from requiredEngineCapabilities.
  Real execution remains deferred by this contract.
- **VALIDATED ARTIFACTS ARE IMMUTABLE.** Registry records, evidence arrays,
  requiredFacets and scopes are deep-frozen, with mutation-attempt tests.

### Cross-PR integration boundary — actual state, not aspiration

`obligationId` is `obl:::<sourceRef>:::<locator>:::<facet>`. PR #477 emits and
validates the same shape at head 71d4eed, so #475 and #477 are mechanically
joinable on this key. PR #476 does NOT participate: it uses
`MembershipIdentity{recordKey, clauseId?, path?, sourceSpan?}` with no
obligationId, and bridging it is deferred to eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7. The ADR states
this gap rather than claiming alignment that does not exist.

closure, mutation and T1-T8 requirements BELOW the scope-reduction section.

That is the supervisor's error and the second time this cycle: after the
decomposition I APPENDED a scope-reduction section instead of REMOVING what it

contains. The same mistake produced the stale 4/64 membership state on
eshyra-o9bd.19.1.6.

Rule going forward: when scope is reduced, the contract is REWRITTEN, not
annotated. A section saying "X moved out" beneath a section still requiring X is
not a correction.

  uniqueness across synthetic scalar and projected atom IDs — is owned by
  eshyra-o9bd.19.1.12 and is blocked on a real source census (eshyra-s38f).
- SCOPE and AGGREGATE CLOSURE — branded scopes proving authoritative membership
  and record ownership, and closure evaluating the same contract as per-clause
  evaluation — is owned by eshyra-o9bd.19.1.13.
- Rationale: the registry was asked to be authoritative while nothing
  underwrote its authority, because the source census is deferred. Mutable
  tables, an evidence taxonomy with no home for known-missing clauses, partial
  multi-part capture, colliding identities and unprovable scope membership were
  symptoms of that, not independent defects.
- This PR now delivers the clause completeness CONTRACT only. obligations.ts is
  a 13-line non-authoritative ObligationSource lookup interface; no validating
  stub remains that could read as authoritative.

### Source obligation
- Source membership: obligations held in an `ObligationRegistry`, keyed
  `obl:::<sourceRef>:::<locator>:::<facet>`, for the scope under evaluation.
  Never the set a projector happened to emit.
- Membership derivation: `ObligationOrigin` is the closed union
  `source-extraction | curated-specification | audit-finding`. It cannot be
  `projector`, so a producer can never be the authority for which obligations
  existed. Every identity component is validated against origin-appropriate
  evidence; synthetic locator divergence is rejected.
- Source spans or authoritative inputs: `ObligationEvidence` of kind
  `source-span` or `authoritative-input`. Repeated clauses at one anchor carry a
  stable occurrence locator so they remain distinguishable.
- Complete obligations covered: this bead defines the obligation BOUNDARY, the
  facet vocabulary, and closure evaluation. Enumerating the SRD corpus's
  obligations is `eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1`.

### Pack or artifact representation
- ONE OBLIGATION PER CLAUSE is the load-bearing invariant. A clause discharges
  exactly one source obligation; that obligation may carry many facets. Source
  material with separable mechanics decomposes into multiple clauses. Enforced
  by `missing-obligation-reference` and `multiple-obligation-references`.
- Required semantic distinctions: composable facets, never universal clause-kind
  assumptions. A specialized facet transitively implies its base mechanic
  (`FACET_IMPLICATIONS`), so `save-with-damage` cannot certify `saves: []`.
- Branches and alternatives: the exclusion graph is validated for symmetry and
  partition; branches and alternatives bind to projected atom identities and may
  target scalar mechanics as well as shells.
- Timing, lifecycle, and termination: `duration`, `recurrence`, `repeatChecks`,
  `immunityWindows` and `termination` are canonical facets, required exactly
  when an obligation declares them.
- Provenance and ownership: `identity`, `sourceSpans`, `provenance`,
  `semanticOwner` and `recordOwner` are canonical base requirements applied to
  every obligation. They cannot be removed or overridden; extensions are
  additive only, and no caller-supplied contract can weaken them.

### Cross-kind and cross-surface checks
- Related kinds or subsystems: all fifteen mechanics-bearing record families
  carry applicability contracts; facets are shared across kinds so one mechanic
  cannot be modelled twice with divergent semantics.
- Corpus-wide predicates: `evaluateObligationClosure` consumes an OPAQUE
  validated scope — a raw object literal cannot be passed — enforces exact
  family and record ownership, reports unexpected claims, and reports UNCLAIMED
  obligations. Family applicability, obligation membership, per-obligation
  completeness and aggregate family closure are four distinct concepts.

### Engine capability
- Required capabilities: `EngineCapability` is the closed union
  `engine:F1`..`engine:F10`, validated.
- Existing owner beads: the ten family epics under `eshyra-olc5`. They retain
  historical `eshyra-o9bd.19.5.*` IDs, so ownership is judged by actual bead
  identity and never by ID prefix.
- Known missing capability handling: capability resolution failures report
  against SUPPORTED, never PROJECTED. A clause may be semantically complete and
  unsupported; that distinction is the point. Stored capability evidence cannot
  drift from `requiredEngineCapabilities`.

### Reference execution or executable proof
- Real artifact or pack-driven scenarios: deliberately out of scope. This bead
  is design and type contract only; `CapabilityResolver`, `SourceEvidenceResolver`
  and `DiscoveryResolver` are injected interfaces with test doubles, so the
  evaluator consumes evidence it cannot forge.
- Negative and fail-closed scenarios: adversarial tests T1-T8, each named for the
  threat it defeats; an unremovable base-requirement removal matrix; generated
  removal tests for every specialized facet; audit-only and known-missing
  CAPTURED rejection; mutation attempts against deep-frozen artifacts.
- CAPTURED is satisfiable only by `source-span` or `authoritative-input`
  evidence. `audit-finding` and `known-missing-source-clause` evidence identify
  a gap and can never close one.
- Replay, rollback, determinism: not in scope; they belong to engine
  certification under `eshyra-olc5.2`.

### Approved residuals
- Source ambiguities: the three deliberate ambiguities remain under
  `eshyra-jhpt.6` / `.7`.
- Deliberately model-adjudicated boundaries: the `model-adjudication` facet.
- Explicitly unsupported scope, each owned by a named bead and NOT a defect in
  this PR:
  - exact source VALUES and relationships — `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.10`. The authority
    here states semantic shapes; encoding values (save ability and DC, damage
    amount, target count, duration unit, reset timing, transition payload)
    requires a source-value model and its extraction.
  - producer and readiness-gate integration — `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.1.2.1`.
  - production census and real resolver implementations — `eshyra-s38f`.
  - cross-PR identity adapters or parity tests — `eshyra-gvzx`.
  - importer migration, corpus recompilation, engine registry implementation.

### Closure evidence
- Generated membership query: `evaluateObligationClosure` over a validated scope.
- Permanent regression evidence: `packages/core/test/clauseIrObligations.test.ts`
  and `packages/core/test/clauseIrContracts.test.ts`.
- Finding-registry aliases: `indep:001`, `opus:F-06`, `opus:F-27`, `sol:CAP-001`.

### Cross-PR integration boundary — actual state
`obligationId` is `obl:::<sourceRef>:::<locator>:::<facet>`. PR #477 emits and
validates the same shape for genuine source obligations and keeps evidence items
in a separate `ev:::` namespace, so #475 and #477 are mechanically joinable.
PR #476 does not participate: it uses
`MembershipIdentity{recordKey, clauseId?, path?, sourceSpan?}` with no
`obligationId`. Bridging it is `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7`. ADR 0020 states this and
does not claim alignment that does not exist.
